title: Fukushima Daiichi Tracker Update — May 16, 2026
summary: TEPCO completed its 19th round of ALPS-treated water ocean discharge in April 2026, with the FY2026 program calling for 8 rounds totaling ~62,400 tonnes — cumulative discharge now exceeds 133,000 m³ since August 2023. In a landmark milestone, TEPCO's Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Unit 6 resumed commercial operations on April 16, 2026, marking the company's first commercial nuclear power generation in approximately 15 years. An April 20 magnitude 7.4–7.7 earthquake triggered precautionary evacuations of workers at both Fukushima Daiichi and Daini, though no plant abnormalities were detected. The IAEA Task Force (May 11–15) confirmed Japan continues to meet all international safety standards for the ALPS discharge program. Japan's third Reconstruction Period (2026–2030) launched in April, with 15 of 32 operable reactors now online.
